title: Grid Matrix Statistics
spec: Write a function `analyze(grid)` that accepts a list of lists of integers and returns a tuple of eight extracted lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the sum of each row, the first element of each row, the maximum value in each row, the rows where every element is strictly positive, the flattened sequence of all even integers in the grid, the absolute values of the elements in the first row, boolean values indicating if a row contains a zero, and the lengths of each row. Example input: [[1, 0], [4, 5]]. Example output: ([1, 9], [1, 4], [1, 5], [[4, 5]], [0, 4], [1, 0], [True, False], [2, 2]).

title: Server Log Parser
spec: Write a function `parse(logs)` that takes a list of string log entries and returns a tuple of eight processed lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the first word of every line, all full lines that include the word error in lowercase, the ip addresses from the second word of lines containing the word timeout, the lengths of log messages having more than fifty characters, the last word of every line, the lines converted to uppercase, boolean values indicating if a line starts with a digit, and the third word of lines containing the word success. Example input: ["12:00 192.0.0.1 error failed"]. Example output: (["12:00"], ["12:00 192.0.0.1 error failed"], [], [], ["failed"], ["12:00 192.0.0.1 ERROR FAILED"], [True], []).

title: Student Grade Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(students)` that takes a list of tuples containing a student name followed by three integer test scores and returns a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the average score for each student, the names of students averaging eighty or higher, the names of students who scored exactly one hundred on any test, the highest score achieved by each student, the names in uppercase for students averaging below fifty, the lowest score for each student, boolean values indicating if the student passed all tests with a score above sixty, and the names of students whose first score is greater than their last. Example input: [("alice", 80, 80, 80)]. Example output: ([80.0], ["alice"], [], [80], [], [80], [True], []).

title: Inventory Restock Checker
spec: Write a function `inventory(items)` that processes a list of tuples containing item name, category, quantity, and unit price, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the names of items with zero quantity, the names of items where total value exceeds one thousand, the names of items in the electronics category, the discounted price at ninety percent for every item, the categories of items costing over fifty dollars, boolean values showing if stock is below ten, the names of items with the word pro in them, and the quantities of items priced under five dollars. Example input: [("tv pro", "electronics", 10, 500)]. Example output: ([], ["tv pro"], ["tv pro"], [450.0], ["electronics"], [False], ["tv pro"], []).

title: Coordinate Geometry Filter
spec: Write a function `geometry(points)` that accepts a list of coordinate tuples representing x and y integer values and returns a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the euclidean distance from the origin for each point, points strictly in the first quadrant, points exactly on either axis, the squared x coordinates for second quadrant points, the points with swapped x and y coordinates, boolean values indicating if the point lies strictly inside a circle of radius six, the sum of x and y for each point, and points where x equals y. Example input: [(3, 4)]. Example output: ([5.0], [(3, 4)], [], [], [(4, 3)], [True], [7], []).

title: Graph Adjacency Processor
spec: Write a function `network(graph)` where the input is a list of lists representing an adjacency list, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the degree of each node, the indices of isolated nodes, the indices of nodes connected to node zero, the neighbors of nodes with exactly one connection, the indices of nodes with self loops, boolean values indicating if the node has more than one neighbor, the squared degree of each node, and the lengths of the neighbor lists formatted as strings. Example input: [[1, 2], [0], []]. Example output: ([2, 1, 0], [2], [1], [0], [], [True, False, False], [4, 1, 0], ["2", "1", "0"]).

title: Shopping Cart Analyzer
spec: Write a function `checkout(carts)` that takes a list of lists containing string product names, and returns a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the total number of items in each cart, the contents of carts having more than five items, the sizes of carts containing a product named apple, the first item of every non-empty cart, all items across all carts converted to uppercase, boolean values showing if the cart contains milk, the last item of every non-empty cart, and the lengths of the first item of every non-empty cart. Example input: [["apple", "banana"]]. Example output: ([2], [], [2], ["apple"], ["APPLE", "BANANA"], [False], ["banana"], [5]).

title: Library Book Sorter
spec: Write a function `library(books)` that takes a list of tuples containing title, author string, publication year, and page count, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the titles of books published after two thousand, the names of authors of books with over five hundred pages, the publication years of books by smith, the title lengths for books published before nineteen ninety, the titles of all books formatted in title case, boolean values indicating if the book is older than fifty years relative to two thousand twenty, the author names in uppercase, and the difference between two thousand twenty and the publication year for each book. Example input: [("dune", "herbert", 1965, 412)]. Example output: ([], [], [], [4], ["Dune"], [True], ["HERBERT"], [55]).

title: Daily Weather Extract
spec: Write a function `weather(forecasts)` that accepts a list of tuples containing a date string, minimum temperature, maximum temperature, and a condition string, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the daily temperature range, the dates of rain days, the maximum temperatures of days with minimum below zero, the conditions of days with range over twenty degrees, the dates in uppercase for snow days, boolean values showing if maximum is above thirty, the average temperature of each day, and the lengths of the condition strings. Example input: [("mon", -5, 10, "snow")]. Example output: ([15], [], [10], [], ["MON"], [False], [2.5], [4]).

title: Financial Transaction Audit
spec: Write a function `finance(transactions)` that processes a list of tuples containing an integer identifier, a transaction type string, a float amount, and a currency string, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the identifiers of deposit transactions, the absolute amounts of withdrawals, the identifiers of transactions over ten thousand, the amounts of euro transactions, the lowercase currencies for transactions under ten absolute, boolean values indicating if the amount is exactly zero, the identifiers of transactions in usd, and the amounts doubled for all transactions. Example input: [(1, "deposit", 500.0, "USD")]. Example output: ([1], [], [], [], [], [False], [1], [1000.0]).

title: Real Estate Property Matcher
spec: Write a function `properties(listings)` that takes a list of tuples containing an address string, bedrooms, bathrooms, and integer price, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the addresses with three or more bedrooms, the prices of two-bathroom properties, the addresses of properties under five hundred thousand, the price per bedroom for properties with at least one bedroom, the addresses capitalized for million-dollar properties, boolean values showing if bathrooms exceed bedrooms, the total rooms calculated as bedrooms plus bathrooms, and the addresses of properties with exactly one bedroom. Example input: [("main st", 3, 2, 400000)]. Example output: (["main st"], [400000], ["main st"], [133333.33333333334], [], [False], [5], []).

title: Chessboard Position Analyzer
spec: Write a function `chessboard(pieces)` that processes a list of tuples containing piece type, color, x coordinate, and y coordinate, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the coordinates of white pieces, the piece types on the fourth rank, the x coordinates of pawns, the coordinates of pieces on the main diagonal, the black piece types in uppercase, boolean values showing if the piece is a knight, the sum of coordinates for each piece, and the colors of pieces on the first file where x is one. Example input: [("pawn", "white", 2, 2)]. Example output: ([(2, 2)], [], [2], [(2, 2)], [], [False], [4], []).

title: File System Scanner
spec: Write a function `filesystem(files)` that takes a list of tuples containing file name, extension, integer size in bytes, and a hidden status boolean, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the names of hidden files, the full filenames for files over one thousand bytes, the sizes of text files with a txt extension, the names of files with empty extensions, the sizes in kilobytes for visible files, boolean values indicating if the size is exactly zero, the file names in uppercase for hidden files, and the lengths of the file extensions. Example input: [("readme", "txt", 500, False)]. Example output: ([], [], [500], [], [0.48828125], [False], [], [3]).

title: Social Media Engagement Feed
spec: Write a function `social(posts)` that processes a list of tuples containing a username, post text, integer likes, and integer shares, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the usernames posting about announcements, the texts of posts with over one hundred likes, the total engagement per post calculated as likes plus shares, the text lengths for zero-share posts, the lowercase usernames for posts with more shares than likes, boolean values showing if engagement exceeds one thousand, the likes doubled for each post, and the usernames of posts with exactly ten likes. Example input: [("Admin", "announcement today", 150, 20)]. Example output: (["Admin"], ["announcement today"], [170], [], [], [False], [300], []).

title: Music Playlist Formatter
spec: Write a function `playlist(songs)` that accepts a list of tuples containing title, artist, genre, and duration in seconds, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the titles of rock songs, the durations in minutes for all songs, the titles of songs over three hundred seconds, the artists of songs with love in the title, the titles of mozart songs, boolean values indicating if the genre is jazz, the durations in seconds for pop songs, and the lengths of the artist names. Example input: [("love me do", "beatles", "rock", 142)]. Example output: (["love me do"], [2.3666666666666667], [], ["beatles"], [], [False], [], [7]).

title: Recipe Ingredient Calculator
spec: Write a function `nutrition(ingredients)` that takes a list of tuples containing ingredient name, measurement unit, float amount, and integer calories per unit, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the total calories per ingredient, the names of ingredients in grams, the names of ingredients over two hundred total calories, the amounts of ingredients with sugar in the name, the uppercase names of low-calorie ingredients under ten calories per unit, boolean values showing if the amount is exactly one, the unit strings in uppercase, and the calorie density per unit doubled. Example input: [("white sugar", "grams", 100.0, 4)]. Example output: ([400.0], ["white sugar"], ["white sugar"], [100.0], ["WHITE SUGAR"], [False], ["GRAMS"], [8]).

title: Public Transit Routines
spec: Write a function `transit(routes)` that processes a list of tuples containing an integer route number, origin string, destination string, and integer travel time in minutes, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the route numbers from central station, the destinations of routes under thirty minutes, the durations in hours for airport routes, the route numbers with identical origin and destination, the origins of routes over sixty minutes, boolean values showing if the route number is even, the travel times in seconds, and the lengths of the destination strings. Example input: [(10, "central station", "airport", 45)]. Example output: ([10], [], [0.75], [], [], [True], [2700], [7]).

title: Hotel Reservation Summary
spec: Write a function `hotel(bookings)` that accepts a list of tuples containing a guest name, room type string, integer number of nights, and float total cost, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the names of suite guests, the nightly rates for each booking, the room types for stays over seven nights, the names of guests spending over one thousand, the guest name lengths for one-night stays, boolean values indicating if the room type is standard, the total costs discounted by ten percent, and the nights squared for each booking. Example input: [("smith", "suite", 3, 900.0)]. Example output: (["smith"], [300.0], [], [], [], [False], [810.0], [9]).

title: Sensor Telemetry Dashboard
spec: Write a function `telemetry(readings)` that processes a list of tuples containing an integer timestamp, string sensor identifier, float temperature, and float humidity, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the timestamps of high humidity readings over eighty percent, the temperatures from the outdoor sensor, the sensor identifiers with below-freezing temperatures, the heat index approximations calculated as temperature plus humidity, the capitalized sensors for early readings before one thousand, boolean values showing if temperature equals humidity, the timestamps converted to strings, and the humidity values halved. Example input: [(900, "outdoor", -2.5, 85.0)]. Example output: ([900], [-2.5], ["outdoor"], [82.5], ["OUTDOOR"], [False], ["900"], [42.5]).

title: Cinema Showing Analyzer
spec: Write a function `cinema(showings)` that takes a list of tuples containing movie title, integer screen number, integer tickets sold, and integer room capacity, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the titles on screen one, the available seats per showing, the titles of sold-out movies, the screen numbers less than half sold, the uppercase titles of large capacity showings over two hundred, boolean values indicating if tickets sold are single digits, the capacities of all showings on screen two, and the lengths of the movie titles. Example input: [("matrix", 1, 100, 100)]. Example output: (["matrix"], [0], ["matrix"], [], [], [False], [], [6]).

title: Fitness Tracker Exporter
spec: Write a function `fitness(workouts)` that accepts a list of tuples containing a date string, activity type, integer duration in minutes, and average heart rate, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the dates of running activities, the durations of high heart rate workouts over one hundred fifty, the activity types over sixty minutes, the estimated calories burned calculated as duration times ten, the dates of low heart rate activities under one hundred, boolean values showing if the activity is yoga, the durations in seconds, and the heart rates halved as floats. Example input: [("monday", "running", 30, 160)]. Example output: (["monday"], [30], [], [300], [], [False], [1800], [80.0]).

title: Email Inbox Filter
spec: Write a function `inbox(emails)` that processes a list of tuples containing sender address, subject string, integer size in kilobytes, and a boolean indicating if it has been read, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the senders of unread emails, the subjects of emails over ten kilobytes, the sizes of urgent emails, the sender address lengths of read emails, the senders of emails with empty subjects, boolean values indicating if the size is exactly one, the subjects converted to uppercase, and the sizes in bytes. Example input: [("boss@work", "urgent meeting", 15, False)]. Example output: (["boss@work"], ["urgent meeting"], [15], [], [], [False], ["URGENT MEETING"], [15360]).

title: Wildlife Sightings Log
spec: Write a function `wildlife(sightings)` that takes a list of tuples containing species name, park zone string, integer number of animals seen, and time of day string, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the species in the north zone, the morning animal counts, the zones with packs over five animals, the uppercase species of night sightings, the first letter of each species, boolean values showing if exactly one animal was seen, the species strings reversed, and the lengths of the zone names. Example input: [("lion", "north", 3, "morning")]. Example output: (["lion"], [3], [], [], ["l"], [False], ["noil"], [5]).

title: Repository Commit History
spec: Write a function `repository(commits)` that processes a list of tuples containing a string hash, author name, integer files changed, and integer lines added, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the hashes by admin, the authors of single-file commits, the lines added for commits over ten files, the hashes of zero-addition commits, the commit hash lengths, boolean values indicating if lines added exceed one hundred, the author names in lowercase, and the files changed doubled. Example input: [("a1b2", "admin", 1, 50)]. Example output: (["a1b2"], ["admin"], [], [], [4], [False], ["admin"], [2]).

title: Astronomical Star Catalog
spec: Write a function `astronomy(stars)` that takes a list of tuples containing star name, constellation name, float apparent magnitude, and float distance in lightyears, returning a tuple of eight lists. The lists must sequentially contain: the names of orion stars, the distances of negative magnitude stars, the constellations of close stars under ten lightyears, the absolute magnitude approximations calculated by subtracting five from apparent magnitude, the uppercase names of far stars over one thousand lightyears, boolean values showing if the distance is exactly zero, the apparent magnitudes converted to integers, and the lengths of the constellation names. Example input: [("sirius", "canis major", -1.46, 8.6)]. Example output: ([], [8.6], ["canis major"], [-6.46], [], [False], [-1], [11]).

title: Tournament Results Processor
spec: Write a module for analyzing sports tournament matches using several helper functions. The first helper processes a list of match tuples containing home team, away team, home goals, and away goals. It must first build a list of all home teams, then build a list of all away teams, and return both. The second helper must first calculate a list of total goals per match, then calculate a list of goal differences per match by subtracting away goals from home goals, and return them. The third helper must first filter the matches to create a list of draws, then create a list of home team wins, and return them. The fourth helper must first isolate matches with more than three total goals, then isolate matches involving the specific team named tigers, and return them. Finally, write an entry function `process(matches)` that calls these helpers and returns a single tuple combining all eight resulting lists. For example, given [('Lions', 'Tigers', 2, 2)], the output is (['Lions'], ['Tigers'], [4], [0], [('Lions', 'Tigers', 2, 2)], [], [('Lions', 'Tigers', 2, 2)], [('Lions', 'Tigers', 2, 2)]).

title: Network Packet Sniffer
spec: Write a module for analyzing network traffic with several helper functions. The first helper processes a list of packet tuples containing source address, destination address, protocol, payload size, and error flag. It must first build a list of source addresses, then build a list of destination addresses, and return both. The second helper must first filter the packets to create a list of packets using the tcp protocol, then create a list of packets using the udp protocol, and return them. The third helper must first calculate a list of payload sizes in kilobytes by dividing by one thousand, then extract a list of the error flags, and return them. The fourth helper must first isolate packets with payload sizes greater than one thousand bytes, then isolate packets originating from the address localhost, and return them. Finally, write an entry function `analyze(packets)` that calls these helpers and returns a single tuple combining all eight resulting lists. For example, given [('localhost', 'remote', 'tcp', 1500, False)], the output is (['localhost'], ['remote'], [('localhost', 'remote', 'tcp', 1500, False)], [], [1.5], [False], [('localhost', 'remote', 'tcp', 1500, False)], [('localhost', 'remote', 'tcp', 1500, False)]).

title: Recipe Nutritional Calculator
spec: Write a module to evaluate nutritional data using helper functions. The first helper processes a list of ingredient tuples containing name, category, calories, fat grams, and protein grams. It must first build a list of names, then build a list of categories, and return both. The second helper must first calculate a list of doubled calories for all ingredients, then calculate a list of doubled protein grams, and return them. The third helper must first filter ingredients to create a list of those categorized as vegetable, then create a list of those with zero fat grams, and return them. The fourth helper must first isolate ingredients with more than two hundred calories, then isolate ingredients with less than fifty calories, and return them. Finally, write an entry function `evaluate(ingredients)` that calls these helpers and returns a single tuple combining all eight resulting lists. For example, given [('Carrot', 'vegetable', 40, 0, 1)], the output is (['Carrot'], ['vegetable'], [80], [2], [('Carrot', 'vegetable', 40, 0, 1)], [('Carrot', 'vegetable', 40, 0, 1)], [], [('Carrot', 'vegetable', 40, 0, 1)]).

title: Employee Timesheet Analyzer
spec: Write a module for auditing employee timesheets using helper functions. The first helper processes a list of daily record tuples containing employee name, department, regular hours, overtime hours, and absence status. It must first build a list of employee names, then build a list of departments, and return both. The second helper must first calculate a list of regular pay amounts at twenty per hour, then calculate a list of overtime pay amounts at thirty per hour, and return them. The third helper must first filter records to create a list of those with a true absence status, then create a list of those with zero overtime hours, and return them. The fourth helper must first isolate records from the engineering department, then isolate records where regular hours exceed eight, and return them. Finally, write an entry function `audit(records)` that calls these helpers and returns a single tuple combining all eight resulting lists. For example, given [('Alice', 'sales', 8, 0, False)], the output is (['Alice'], ['sales'], [160], [0], [], [('Alice', 'sales', 8, 0, False)], [], []).

title: Traffic Camera Parser
spec: Write a module for monitoring traffic camera data using helper functions. The first helper processes a list of vehicle record tuples containing license plate, vehicle type, speed, speed limit, and lane number. It must first build a list of license plates, then build a list of vehicle types, and return both. The second helper must first calculate a list of differences between speed and speed limit, then calculate a list of speeds in kilometers per hour by multiplying by one point six, and return them. The third helper must first filter records to create a list of those exceeding the speed limit by more than ten, then create a list of those in lane one, and return them. The fourth helper must first isolate records for the vehicle type truck, then isolate records with speeds below forty, and return them. Finally, write an entry function `monitor(vehicles)` that calls these helpers and returns a single tuple combining all eight resulting lists. For example, given [('ABC', 'car', 65, 50, 1)], the output is (['ABC'], ['car'], [15], [104.0], [('ABC', 'car', 65, 50, 1)], [('ABC', 'car', 65, 50, 1)], [], []).

title: Geometry Polygon Processor
spec: Write a module for processing two dimensional line segments using helper functions. The first helper processes a list of segment tuples containing start x, start y, end x, and end y coordinates. It must first build a list of start x coordinates, then build a list of end y coordinates, and return both. The second helper must first calculate a list of horizontal spans using absolute differences, then calculate a list of vertical spans using absolute differences, and return them. The third helper must first filter segments to create a list of horizontal lines where start y equals end y, then create a list of vertical lines where start x equals end x, and return them. The fourth helper must first isolate segments starting exactly at zero for both x and y, then isolate segments with a start x greater than ten, and return them. Finally, write an entry function `process(segments)` that calls these helpers and returns a single tuple combining all eight resulting lists. For example, given [(0, 0, 5, 0)], the output is ([0], [0], [5], [0], [(0, 0, 5, 0)], [], [(0, 0, 5, 0)], []).

title: Course Enrollment Validator
spec: Write a module for validating student course enrollments using helper functions. The first helper processes a list of student record tuples containing student name, major, completed credits, current credits, and probation status. It must first build a list of student names, then build a list of majors, and return both. The second helper must first calculate a list of total projected credits by adding completed and current credits, then calculate a list of remaining credits needed to reach one hundred twenty by subtracting completed from one hundred twenty, and return them. The third helper must first filter records to create a list of students on probation, then create a list of students with current credits over fifteen, and return them. The fourth helper must first isolate students majoring in physics, then isolate students with zero completed credits, and return them. Write an entry function `validate(students)` that calls these helpers and returns a single tuple combining all eight resulting lists. For example, given [('Bob', 'physics', 0, 16, True)], the output is (['Bob'], ['physics'], [16], [120], [('Bob', 'physics', 0, 16, True)], [('Bob', 'physics', 0, 16, True)], [('Bob', 'physics', 0, 16, True)], [('Bob', 'physics', 0, 16, True)]).

title: E-commerce Order Packer
spec: Write a module for planning order packaging using helper functions. The first helper processes a list of item tuples containing item name, warehouse zone, weight, volume, and fragility flag. It must first build a list of item names, then build a list of warehouse zones, and return both. The second helper must first calculate a list of shipping costs by multiplying weight by five, then calculate a list of space densities by dividing weight by volume, and return them. The third helper must first filter items to create a list of fragile ones, then create a list of items located in zone alpha, and return them. The fourth helper must first isolate heavy items weighing more than fifty, then isolate bulky items with volume over one hundred, and return them. Write an entry function `pack(items)` that calls these helpers and returns a single tuple combining all eight resulting lists. For example, given [('Vase', 'alpha', 10, 5, True)], the output is (['Vase'], ['alpha'], [50], [2.0], [('Vase', 'alpha', 10, 5, True)], [('Vase', 'alpha', 10, 5, True)], [], []).

title: Plant Growth Tracker
spec: Write a module for tracking botanical greenhouse growth using helper functions. The first helper processes a list of plant record tuples containing species, section, initial height, current height, and high water need flag. It must first build a list of species, then build a list of sections, and return both. The second helper must first calculate a list of absolute height growth by subtracting initial from current height, then extract a list of the high water need flags, and return them. The third helper must first filter plants to create a list of those requiring high water, then create a list of those located in the north section, and return them. The fourth helper must first isolate plants that grew more than ten units, then isolate plants that did not grow at all, and return them. Write an entry function `track(plants)` that calls these helpers and returns a single tuple combining all eight resulting lists. For example, given [('Fern', 'north', 20, 35, True)], the output is (['Fern'], ['north'], [15], [True], [('Fern', 'north', 20, 35, True)], [('Fern', 'north', 20, 35, True)], [('Fern', 'north', 20, 35, True)], []).

title: Customer Survey Compiler
spec: Write a module for compiling customer survey results using helper functions. The first helper processes a list of response tuples containing respondent name, country, satisfaction score, quality score, and recommendation flag. It must first build a list of names, then build a list of countries, and return both. The second helper must first calculate a list of total combined scores by adding satisfaction and quality scores, then extract a list of the recommendation flags, and return them. The third helper must first filter responses to create a list of those recommending the product, then create a list of responses from japan, and return them. The fourth helper must first isolate responses with a perfect satisfaction score of ten, then isolate those with quality scores below five, and return them. Write an entry function `compile(responses)` that calls these helpers and returns a single tuple combining all eight resulting lists. For example, given [('Ken', 'japan', 10, 4, True)], the output is (['Ken'], ['japan'], [14], [True], [('Ken', 'japan', 10, 4, True)], [('Ken', 'japan', 10, 4, True)], [('Ken', 'japan', 10, 4, True)], [('Ken', 'japan', 10, 4, True)]).

title: Supply Chain Router
spec: Write a module for analyzing supply chain delivery routes using helper functions. The first helper processes a list of route tuples containing driver name, vehicle type, distance, expected hours, and delay status. It must first build a list of driver names, then build a list of vehicle types, and return both. The second helper must first calculate a list of average speeds by dividing distance by expected hours, then calculate a list of safety buffers by multiplying expected hours by zero point one, and return them. The third helper must first filter routes to create a list of those currently delayed, then create a list of routes using a van, and return them. The fourth helper must first isolate long routes exceeding five hundred in distance, then isolate quick routes with expected hours under two, and return them. Write an entry function `route(deliveries)` that calls these helpers and returns a single tuple combining all eight resulting lists. For example, given [('Sue', 'van', 600, 10, True)], the output is (['Sue'], ['van'], [60.0], [1.0], [('Sue', 'van', 600, 10, True)], [('Sue', 'van', 600, 10, True)], [('Sue', 'van', 600, 10, True)], []).

title: Flight Delay Investigator
spec: Write a module for investigating commercial flight delays using helper functions. The first helper processes a list of flight tuples containing airline, flight number, scheduled departure, actual departure, and weather warning flag. It must first build a list of airlines, then build a list of flight numbers, and return both. The second helper must first calculate a list of delay durations by subtracting scheduled from actual departure, then extract a list of the weather warning flags, and return them. The third helper must first filter flights to create a list of those with weather warnings, then create a list of those departing exactly on time with zero delay, and return them. The fourth helper must first isolate severely delayed flights with delays over sixty, then isolate flights operated by skyline, and return them. Write an entry function `investigate(flights)` that calls these helpers and returns a single tuple combining all eight resulting lists. For example, given [('skyline', 101, 800, 870, True)], the output is (['skyline'], [101], [70], [True], [('skyline', 101, 800, 870, True)], [], [('skyline', 101, 800, 870, True)], [('skyline', 101, 800, 870, True)]).

title: Cinema Seat Allocator
spec: Write a module for analyzing cinema seating using helper functions. The first helper processes a list of seat tuples containing row letter, seat number, base price, booking status, and wheelchair accessibility. It must first build a list of row letters, then build a list of seat numbers, and return both. The second helper must first calculate a list of discounted prices by multiplying base price by zero point eight, then calculate a list of luxury prices by adding ten to the base price, and return them. The third helper must first filter seats to create a list of available seats where booking status is false, then create a list of seats that are wheelchair accessible, and return them. title: Trebuchet Ballistics Simulator
spec: The entry function is `launch(parameters)`. The input is a list of tuples containing projectile mass, counterweight mass, and release angle. First, create a list extracting all projectile masses and filter the parameters to build a list of valid launches where counterweight mass exceeds projectile mass. Next, calculate lists of mass ratios and theoretical ranges for each valid launch using the ratio and angle. Then, filter the ranges to produce a list of successful shots traveling at least one hundred meters, extracting their release angles and converting them to a list of radians. Finally, generate a list of formatted trajectory warning strings for each successful launch, returning a tuple of the mass ratios, successful ranges, and warning strings.

title: Lighthouse Flash Sequence Analyzer
spec: The entry function is `analyze(flashes)`. The input is a list of flash durations in seconds. First, filter the input to build a list of valid durations over one second and round each to create a list of nearest whole seconds. Next, filter the rounded durations to build separate lists of short flashes measuring exactly one second and long flashes of three seconds or more. Then, convert each rounded duration into a list of morse code dot or dash characters, and calculate differences between adjacent flashes to generate a list of interval durations. Finally, filter the intervals to produce a list of long breaks exceeding five seconds and build a list of timestamp strings for each recorded valid flash, returning the morse characters, long intervals, and timestamps.

title: Sushi Conveyor Belt Tracker
spec: The entry function is `bill(plates)`. The input is a list of tuples containing plate color, customer seat number, and elapsed minutes on the belt. First, create a list extracting the colors of all plates, and filter the input to build separate lists of plates consumed by seat one and seat two. Next, calculate a list of base prices for each plate based on its color, and filter the input to produce a list of old plates on the belt for more than ten minutes. Then, calculate a list of discounted prices for the old plates by reducing their base price by twenty percent. Finally, create separate lists of line item descriptions for seat one and seat two combining the color and price, returning a tuple of these two description lists.

title: Juggling Pattern Siteswap Validator
spec: The entry function is `validate(throws)`. The input is a list of integers representing juggling throw heights. First, filter the input to build a list of active non-zero throws, then separate these into lists of even numbers for same-hand throws and odd numbers for crossing throws. Next, calculate a list of landing times for each throw by adding its height to its sequence index, and compute a list of landing beats using a modulo of the total number of throws. Then, generate a list of catch heights by subtracting one from each original throw, and filter the active throws to produce a list of high throws strictly greater than three. Finally, build a list of choreographic sequence strings turning each integer into a text action, returning the landing beats, catch heights, and sequence strings.

title: Crop Circle Geometry Extractor
spec: The entry function is `measure(nodes)`. The input is a list of tuples containing radial distance, angular position, and flattening intensity. First, create a list extracting all radial distances, and filter the nodes to build a list of intense nodes with flattening intensity exceeding eighty percent. Next, create a list extracting the angular positions of intense nodes and calculate a list of circumferences using their radial distances. Then, filter the intense nodes to build separate lists of inner ring nodes under fifty meters and outer ring nodes of fifty meters or more. Finally, convert the inner ring angular positions to a list of radians, and generate a list of classification label strings for all nodes, returning the inner ring nodes, outer ring nodes, and labels.

title: Domino Chain Reaction Simulator
spec: The entry function is `topple(dominoes)`. The input is a list of tuples containing domino height, spacing to the next domino, and material weight. First, create a list extracting all domino heights, then filter the sequence into a list of successful strikes where spacing is less than height and a list of failed strikes where spacing exceeds height. Next, calculate lists of fall durations based on height and weight, and extract the material weights of dominoes involved in successful strikes. Then, compute a list of kinetic energy values transferred during each successful strike and generate a list of cumulative fall times by summing previous durations. Finally, create a list of visual text representations of the falling sequence using slashes and vertical bars, returning the successful strikes, kinetic energies, and text representations.

title: Fireworks Display Choreographer
spec: The entry function is `schedule(shells)`. The input is a list of tuples containing shell diameter, lift charge amount, and color code. First, create a list extracting all shell diameters, and filter the input into lists of heavy shells over six inches and light shells of six inches or less. Next, calculate a list of expected burst altitudes using the lift charge amount, and determine a list of fuse delay times for each shell based on altitude. Then, create a list extracting the color codes for heavy shells and format a list of launch command strings combining delay time and color code. Finally, generate a list of safety perimeter radii by multiplying each diameter by ten, returning the heavy shells, launch commands, and safety radii.

title: Sandcastle Structural Integrity
spec: The entry function is `assess(towers)`. The input is a list of tuples containing base radius, tower height, and sand moisture percentage. First, create a list extracting all tower heights, calculate a list of base areas using the base radius, and compute a list of volumes from the area and height. Next, filter the input into a list of structurally sound towers with ten to twenty percent moisture, and a list of collapse risks falling outside this range. Then, create a list extracting the heights of the structurally sound towers and calculate a list of maximum load capacities based on volume and moisture. Finally, generate a list of aesthetic rating strings for the sound towers based on height, returning the sound towers, load capacities, and aesthetic ratings.

title: Elevator Traffic Floor Analyzer
spec: The entry function is `route(requests)`. The input is a list of tuples containing origin floor, destination floor, and passenger count. First, create lists extracting all origin floors and all destination floors, then filter the input into a list of upward journeys and a list of downward journeys. Next, calculate a list of distances traveled in floors for each upward journey and extract a list of passenger counts for all downward journeys. Then, compute a list of total weight loads for each journey assuming an average person weight. Finally, generate a list of floor display text strings for the elevator screen indicating the next stop, returning the upward journeys, downward passenger counts, and display texts.

title: Hydroelectric Dam Sluice Controller
spec: The entry function is `sluice(gates)`. The input is a list of tuples containing gate width, current water flow, and debris accumulation level. First, create a list extracting all water flows, filter the input to build a list of clogged gates with high debris, and extract their widths into a separate list. Next, calculate a list of required opening angles based on water flow, and generate a list of projected water volumes for each gate over the next hour. Then, filter the input to produce a list of clean gates where debris is minimal, and create a list of maintenance warning strings for the clogged gates. Finally, build a list of control command strings combining the gate index and opening angle, returning the opening angles, warnings, and control commands.

title: Watch Escapement Gear Ratios
spec: The entry function is `calibrate(gears)`. The input is a list of tuples containing driving gear teeth, driven gear teeth, and base rotational speed. First, create a list extracting driving gear teeth counts, and calculate a list of mechanical advantage ratios by dividing driven teeth by driving teeth. Next, filter the input into a list of step down configurations with more driven teeth and a list of step up configurations with fewer driven teeth. Then, calculate a list of resulting rotational speeds for each driven gear and extract the speeds of the step down configurations into a separate list. Finally, calculate a list of torque multipliers for each gear pair and generate a list of assembly instruction strings, returning the step down configurations, driven speeds, and assembly instructions.

title: Drone Swarm Formation Controller
spec: The entry function is `navigate(drones)`. The input is a list of tuples containing horizontal coordinate, vertical coordinate, and battery percentage. First, create a list extracting all horizontal coordinates and calculate a list of distances from the origin center point for each drone. Next, filter the input into a list of drifting drones beyond fifty meters and a list of low battery drones with under twenty percent power. Then, calculate a list of return vector coordinates for the drifting drones and extract a list of vertical coordinates for drones with sufficient battery. Finally, compute a list of required charging times for low battery drones and generate a list of flight command strings, returning the drifting drones, return vectors, and flight commands.

title: Braille Document Paginator
spec: The entry function is `paginate(paragraphs)`. The input is a list of strings representing text paragraphs. First, calculate a list of character lengths for each paragraph and filter the input to build a list of valid paragraphs by removing any that contain only whitespace. Next, compute a list of required braille cell counts accounting for capital letters and numbers, and calculate a list of physical braille lines needed assuming forty cells per line. Then, filter the valid paragraphs into lists of short paragraphs fitting on a single line and long paragraphs requiring multiple lines. Finally, create a list extracting the first ten characters of each valid paragraph as a preview and generate a list of pagination marker strings, returning the cell counts, short paragraphs, and pagination markers.

title: Pinball Machine Playfield Scoring
spec: The entry function is `tally(events)`. The input is a list of tuples containing target name, base points, and current multiplier. First, create a list extracting the base points of all events and calculate a list of total scored points by multiplying base points by the multiplier. Next, filter the input into a list of high scoring events awarding over ten thousand points and a list of low scoring events awarding under one thousand points. Then, create a list extracting the target names of high scoring events and calculate a list of bonus points earned purely from multipliers for each event. Finally, convert all target names into a list of uppercase strings and generate a list of animated text callout strings for high scoring events, returning the total scores, high scoring names, and callouts.

title: Harmonica Tablature Transcriber
spec: The entry function is `transcribe(notes)`. The input is a list of tuples containing musical pitch, duration, and playing technique. First, create a list extracting all musical pitches, then filter the input into a list of blow notes requiring exhaling and a list of draw notes requiring inhaling. Next, map each pitch to create a list of corresponding harmonica hole numbers, extract a list of draw note durations, and filter the input to build a list of bent notes. Then, calculate a list of required breath pressure intensities for each note based on pitch and duration. Finally, generate a list of formatted tablature strings combining the hole number, technique symbol, and duration markers, returning the blow notes, draw notes, and tablature strings.

title: Steampunk Boiler Pressure Regulator
spec: The entry function is `regulate(valves)`. The input is a list of tuples containing valve diameter, steam flow rate, and structural integrity rating. First, create a list extracting valve diameters and calculate a list of internal pressures using the flow rate and diameter. Next, filter the input into a list of safe valves where pressure is below the integrity rating and a list of critical valves where it exceeds the rating. Then, compute a list of required pressure release amounts for each critical valve and extract a list of flow rates from the safe valves. Finally, calculate a list of emergency shutoff times for critical valves and generate a list of maintenance log strings detailing valve status, returning the safe valves, critical valves, and logs.

title: Kite Aerial Photography Surveyor
spec: The entry function is `survey(flights)`. The input is a list of tuples containing string length, wind angle in degrees, and camera weight. First, create a list extracting string lengths and calculate a list of vertical altitudes using string length and the sine of the wind angle. Next, filter the input into a list of stable flights with wind angles over forty five degrees and a list of unstable flights with lower angles. Then, calculate a list of lifting forces generated during stable flights and create a list extracting the camera weights of unstable flights. Finally, compute a list of theoretical maximum altitudes for zero camera weight and generate a list of topographical mapping label strings, returning the vertical altitudes, stable flights, and mapping labels.

title: Typewriter Ribbon Ink Depletion
spec: The entry function is `typewrite(strokes)`. The input is a list of tuples containing character struck, impact force, and current ribbon position. First, create a list extracting the characters struck and calculate a list of ink volumes consumed based on impact force and character size. Next, filter the input into lists of heavy strokes exceeding a standard threshold and light strokes falling below it. Then, compute a list of remaining ink levels at each ribbon position and create a list extracting the ribbon positions for heavy strokes. Finally, calculate a list of required ribbon advancement distances and generate a list of fading text warning strings for low ink levels, returning the ink consumed, heavy strokes, and warning strings.

title: Water Slide Physics Analyzer
spec: The entry function is `slide(riders)`. The input is a list of tuples containing rider weight, starting height, and friction coefficient. First, create a list extracting rider weights and calculate a list of potential energies for each rider at their starting height. Next, filter the input into a list of fast riders overcoming friction and a list of slow riders experiencing significant friction drag. Then, calculate a list of splashdown velocities for fast riders and create a list extracting the starting heights of slow riders. Finally, compute a list of total transit times for each rider and generate a list of safety dispatch interval strings, returning the fast riders, splashdown velocities, and dispatch intervals.

title: Escape Artist Padlock Picker
spec: The entry function is `pick(pins)`. The input is a list of tuples containing pin length, spring tension, and current binding status. First, create a list extracting pin lengths and calculate a list of required lifting forces based on length and spring tension. Next, filter the input into a list of bound pins resisting rotation and a list of set pins successfully reaching the shear line. Then, create a list extracting the spring tensions of bound pins and compute a list of optimal pick angles to avoid oversetting them. Finally, calculate a list of feedback click intensities for set pins and generate a list of step by step unlocking sequence strings, returning the bound pins, set pins, and unlocking sequences.

title: Terrarium Microclimate Modeler
spec: The entry function is `simulate(sensors)`. The input is a list of tuples containing soil moisture, ambient light hours, and fungal spore count. First, create a list extracting soil moisture levels and calculate a list of overall humidity indexes for each sensor location. Next, filter the input into a list of healthy zones with optimal balance and a list of mold risk zones with dangerously high spore counts. Then, create a list extracting the ambient light hours of healthy zones and compute a list of required ventilation durations for mold risk zones. Finally, calculate a list of projected plant growth rates for healthy zones and generate a list of automated watering schedule strings, returning the healthy zones, mold risk zones, and watering schedules.

title: Skateboard Trick Combo Scorer
spec: The entry function is `score(tricks)`. The input is a list of tuples containing trick base value, rotation in degrees, and execution stance. First, create a list extracting all trick base values and calculate a list of rotation multipliers by dividing rotation degrees by one hundred and eighty. Next, filter the input into a list of high scoring switch stance tricks and a list of regular stance tricks. Then, calculate a list of final scores by applying multipliers and bonuses, and extract a list of rotations for the switch stance tricks. Finally, compute a list of balance penalties for incomplete rotations and generate a list of announcer shoutout strings for tricks exceeding a master threshold, returning the final scores, switch stance tricks, and shoutouts.

title: Calligraphy Brush Stroke Analyzer
spec: The entry function is `evaluate(strokes)`. The input is a list of tuples containing pressure applied, stroke duration, and ink thickness. First, create a list extracting applied pressures and calculate a list of stroke speeds by dividing stroke length by duration. Next, filter the input into a list of elegant strokes with smooth tapering and a list of blotchy strokes with excessive pooling. Then, create a list extracting ink thicknesses of elegant strokes and compute a list of required drying times for blotchy strokes. Finally, calculate a list of aesthetic harmony scores for elegant strokes and generate a list of critique feedback strings, returning the elegant strokes, blotchy strokes, and critique feedback.

title: Glassblowing Kiln Temperature Profiler
spec: The entry function is `anneal(pieces)`. The input is a list of tuples containing glass thickness, color pigment, and current temperature. First, create a list extracting all glass thicknesses and filter the input to build a list of thick pieces exceeding one inch. Next, extract a list of current temperatures from the thick pieces and calculate a list of target cooling rates based on thickness. Then, generate a list of temperature differentials comparing current temperature to room temperature and filter the original input to produce a list of pieces containing cobalt pigment. Finally, create a list of string labels combining pigment and thickness, and build a list of heating schedule step strings, returning the cooling rates, cobalt pieces, and schedule steps.

title: Astrophotography Image Pipeline
spec: Write a data processing pipeline with the entry function `process(exposures)`. The input is a list of tuples where each contains an image name string, an exposure time, a star count, and a noise level. The pipeline must generate a comprehensive report containing eight specific lists. First, extract all image names from the raw input. Second, extract all noise levels. Third, identify valid image names where the noise level is below twenty. Fourth, extract the star counts strictly for those valid images. Fifth, calculate the stellar density by dividing each valid star count by its corresponding exposure time. Sixth, isolate the exposure times of the valid images. Seventh, convert those valid exposure times into milliseconds by multiplying by one thousand. Finally, generate a list of summary strings for the valid images formatted as the image name followed by the word processed. Return a tuple of these eight generated lists. Write a short driver block that creates sample data and passes it to the function. Example input: a list with one tuple containing orion, five, one hundred, ten. Expected output: a tuple of eight lists where the last is a list containing orion processed.

title: Subalpine Flora Survey
spec: Implement an ecological analysis script with the function `analyze(plants)`. The input is a list of tuples detailing plant observations, each containing a species name, an altitude in meters, a petal count, and a soil acidity level. Produce an eight part ecological summary tuple. First, list all species names from the survey. Second, list all altitude readings. Third, filter the species names to include only those found above two thousand meters. Fourth, extract the soil acidity levels for these high altitude observations. Fifth, normalize these acidity levels by multiplying each by zero point nine. Sixth, extract the petal counts for the high altitude plants. Seventh, determine the expected seed yield by multiplying each high altitude petal count by three. Eighth, format a display string for each high altitude observation combining the species name and the word alpine. Return the tuple containing these eight sequences. Include a brief driver block that defines dummy survey data and calls the function. Example input: a list with a tuple of gentian, two thousand five hundred, five, six. Example output: a tuple of eight lists, the last being a list containing gentian alpine.

title: Medieval Manuscript Illuminator
spec: Create a cataloging script starting with the function `catalog(pages)`. The input is a list of tuples representing manuscript pages, containing a chapter name, a gold leaf thickness, a red pigment amount, and a tear count. The analysis must yield eight distinct lists for restoration. First, collect all chapter names. Second, collect all tear counts. Third, isolate the chapter names of pristine pages which have exactly zero tears. Fourth, extract the gold leaf thicknesses for these pristine pages. Fifth, convert these thicknesses from millimeters to micrometers by multiplying by one thousand. Sixth, extract the red pigment amounts for the pristine pages. Seventh, calculate the required binder volume by doubling each pristine red pigment amount. Eighth, create a sequence of storage labels combining the pristine chapter name with the phrase safe storage. Return all eight lists as a single tuple. Include a small driver routine to execute the script with sample data. Example input: genesis, zero point one, five, zero. Example output tuple ends with a list containing genesis safe storage.

title: Amateur Radio Contester
spec: Develop a logbook processor containing the function `process(contacts)`. The input is a sequence of tuples where each holds a station callsign, a frequency in megahertz, a signal strength, and a distance in kilometers. The processor must return an eight element tuple of lists. First, extract all station callsigns. Second, extract all distances. Third, find the callsigns of distant stations where the distance exceeds five hundred. Fourth, extract the frequencies for these distant contacts. Fifth, convert these frequencies to kilohertz by multiplying by one thousand. Sixth, extract the signal strengths for the distant contacts. Seventh, calculate an adjusted strength by adding five to each distant signal strength. Eighth, generate a confirmation message for each distant contact by appending the phrase confirmed dx to the callsign. The function should return these eight lists. Add a main block to run a test case. Example input: station alpha, fourteen, nine, six hundred. The final output list will contain station alpha confirmed dx.

title: Vintage Clockwork Restorer
spec: Write a mechanical analysis tool utilizing the function `evaluate(gears)`. The input is a list of tuples representing clock gears, each with a material name, a teeth count, a radius in millimeters, and a friction coefficient. The tool must output eight separate lists in a tuple. First, list all material names. Second, list all friction coefficients. Third, identify the material names of efficient gears whose friction coefficient is below zero point two. Fourth, extract the teeth counts of these efficient gears. Fifth, compute the rotation ratio by dividing each efficient teeth count by ten. Sixth, extract the radii of the efficient gears. Seventh, calculate the circumference for each efficient gear by multiplying its radius by six point two eight. Eighth, formulate an inventory tag for each efficient gear joining the material name with the word approved. Return the eight sequences. Provide a driver section with sample gear records. Example input: brass, forty, twenty, zero point one. The last list in the tuple will contain brass approved.

title: Deep Core Ice Stratigraphy
spec: Implement a geological script with the entry function `stratify(cores)`. The input is a list of tuples representing ice core layers, containing a region string, a depth in meters, a carbon isotope ratio, and a dust particle count. Generate an eight list diagnostic tuple. First, extract all region strings. Second, extract all dust particle counts. Third, filter the region strings for deep layers where the depth is greater than one hundred meters. Fourth, isolate the carbon isotope ratios for these deep layers. Fifth, normalize the ratios by subtracting zero point five from each. Sixth, extract the dust particle counts specifically for the deep layers. Seventh, estimate the ancient wind speed by multiplying each deep dust count by one point two. Eighth, create a database key for each deep layer by concatenating the region string with the word deep. Return the tuple of these eight sequences. Include a short main execution block. Example input: polar, one hundred fifty, two point zero, ten. The final list returned holds polar deep.

title: Urban Pigeon Tracking
spec: Develop an avian tracking module starting with the function `track(birds)`. The input is a list of tuples for each pigeon, containing a neighborhood string, a flight distance in kilometers, an altitude in meters, and a resting time in minutes. The module must produce eight lists within a tuple. First, retrieve all neighborhood strings. Second, retrieve all resting times. Third, filter the neighborhoods to include only active pigeons whose resting time is under thirty minutes. Fourth, extract the flight distances for these active birds. Fifth, convert these distances to meters by multiplying by one thousand. Sixth, extract the altitudes for the active birds. Seventh, calculate the glide ratio by dividing each active flight distance by its altitude. Eighth, generate a status text for each active bird joining the neighborhood string with the word patrol. Return the tuple of eight lists. Write a driver block to demonstrate functionality. Example input: downtown, five, fifty, twenty. Final list output contains downtown patrol.

title: Lighthouse Lens Calibration
spec: Create an optical adjustment script featuring the function `calibrate(lenses)`. The input is a sequence of tuples representing glass panels, containing a directional sector string, a focal length, a transparency percentage, and a crack count. The script must return eight lists grouped in a tuple. First, compile all directional sector strings. Second, compile all crack counts. Third, filter the sectors to find pristine panels with exactly zero cracks. Fourth, extract the focal lengths for these pristine panels. Fifth, adjust the focal lengths by adding fifteen to each. Sixth, extract the transparency percentages for the pristine panels. Seventh, calculate the light transmission by multiplying each pristine transparency by zero point nine. Eighth, format an inspection label for each pristine panel by appending the word clear to its sector string. Return the eight collected lists. Include a driver to test the function. Example input: north, two hundred, ninety, zero. The eighth list will contain north clear.

title: Haberdashery Suit Tailoring
spec: Write a fabric processing module that includes the function `measure(bolts)`. The input is a list of tuples representing bolts of cloth, containing a color pattern, a length in yards, a thread count, and a defect count. Produce an eight element tuple of lists. First, extract all color patterns. Second, extract all defect counts. Third, isolate the color patterns of premium bolts having fewer than three defects. Fourth, extract the lengths of these premium bolts. Fifth, convert the premium lengths into inches by multiplying by thirty six. Sixth, extract the thread counts of the premium bolts. Seventh, calculate a durability score by multiplying each premium thread count by one point five. Eighth, formulate a catalog string for each premium bolt by combining the color pattern with the phrase premium stock. Return these eight lists. Add a small main section to process dummy data. Example input: houndstooth, ten, two hundred, one. The final list includes houndstooth premium stock.

title: River Delta Silt Depositions
spec: Implement a sediment analysis tool with the function `analyze(samples)`. The input is a list of tuples for soil samples, containing a mineral name, a depth in centimeters, a grain size, and an organic matter percentage. Output an eight list summary tuple. First, collect all mineral names. Second, collect all organic matter percentages. Third, filter the mineral names for surface samples where the depth is less than twenty centimeters. Fourth, extract the grain sizes for these surface samples. Fifth, categorize the grain sizes by multiplying each by two to get a coarseness index. Sixth, extract the organic percentages for the surface samples. Seventh, compute the fertility score by adding ten to each surface organic percentage. Eighth, construct a laboratory label for each surface sample joining the mineral name with the word surface. Return the complete tuple of lists. Write a driver block setting up sample inputs. Example input: quartz, ten, five, two. The eighth list will hold quartz surface.

title: Neon Sign Gas Mixer
spec: Develop a rare gas formulation script starting with the function `mix(tubes)`. The input is a sequence of tuples representing glass tubes, containing a gas name, a volume in milliliters, a pressure reading, and a leakage rate. The script must output eight separate lists in a tuple. First, gather all gas names. Second, gather all leakage rates. Third, identify the gas names of sealed tubes where the leakage rate is strictly zero. Fourth, extract the volumes of these sealed tubes. Fifth, calculate the required electrical charge by multiplying each sealed volume by twelve. Sixth, extract the pressure readings of the sealed tubes. Seventh, normalize the pressures by dividing each by one point zero five. Eighth, create a manufacturing tag for each sealed tube by combining the gas name with the word ready. Return the eight sequences. Provide a main execution block to pass test data. Example input: argon, fifty, one hundred, zero. The final returned list will contain argon ready.

title: Antique Typewriter Key Alignment
spec: Create a mechanical calibration script with the function `align(keys)`. The input is a list of tuples representing typewriter levers, containing a character string, a strike force, a spring tension, and a rust level. Generate an eight part tuple of lists. First, list all character strings. Second, list all rust levels. Third, isolate the characters of salvageable keys whose rust level is below five. Fourth, extract the strike forces for these salvageable keys. Fifth, determine the striking momentum by multiplying each salvageable strike force by one point four. Sixth, extract the spring tensions for the salvageable keys. Seventh, compute the optimal recoil by subtracting two from each salvageable spring tension. Eighth, format a repair ticket for each salvageable key by appending the phrase needs alignment to the character string. Return the tuple containing these eight lists. Include a short driver to test the alignment logic. Example input: letter a, ten, fifteen, two. The final list includes letter a needs alignment.

title: Hydroponic Nutrient Doser
spec: Write an agricultural automation module utilizing the function `dose(plants)`. The input is a sequence of tuples representing crop trays, containing a crop variety, a water volume, a nitrogen level, and a ph imbalance score. Output an eight element tuple of lists. First, extract all crop varieties. Second, extract all ph imbalance scores. Third, filter the crop varieties to include only stable trays where the ph imbalance is less than two. Fourth, extract the water volumes for these stable trays. Fifth, calculate the daily evaporation by multiplying each stable water volume by zero point zero five. Sixth, extract the nitrogen levels of the stable trays. Seventh, determine the required fertilizer drops by multiplying each stable nitrogen level by three. Eighth, construct a daily log string for each stable tray by joining the crop variety with the word balanced. Return these eight lists. Include a main block with sample tray records. Example input: basil, twenty, five, one. The eighth list will hold basil balanced.

title: Choral Harmony Arranger
spec: Implement a vocal arrangement script featuring the function `arrange(voices)`. The input is a list of tuples for singers, containing a vocal part, a maximum pitch frequency, a breath duration, and a slight pitch error margin. The script must return eight distinct lists in a tuple. First, retrieve all vocal parts. Second, retrieve all pitch error margins. Third, identify the vocal parts of accurate singers whose pitch error margin is below three. Fourth, extract the maximum pitch frequencies for these accurate singers. Fifth, transpose the frequencies down an octave by dividing each by two. Sixth, extract the breath durations for the accurate singers. Seventh, calculate the required musical rest periods by subtracting one from each accurate breath duration. Eighth, generate an assignment string for each accurate singer by appending the phrase first chair to their vocal part. Return the full tuple of lists. Write a driver routine to demonstrate the function. Example input: soprano, eight hundred, ten, one. The final output list contains soprano first chair.

title: Stained Glass Window Glazier
spec: Develop an artisanal crafting script starting with the function `glaze(pieces)`. The input is a sequence of tuples representing cut glass, containing a color description, a surface area, a thickness, and a chip count. Produce an eight list tuple for the project. First, collect all color descriptions. Second, collect all chip counts. Third, filter the color descriptions for perfect pieces that have zero chips. Fourth, extract the surface areas of these perfect pieces. Fifth, calculate the required lead frame length by multiplying each perfect surface area by three point one four. Sixth, extract the thicknesses for the perfect pieces. Seventh, determine the flux paste volume by doubling each perfect thickness. Eighth, format a blueprint label for each perfect piece by joining the color description with the word center. Return the tuple containing these eight sequences. Add a small main section to process example glass data. Example input: cobalt blue, ten, five, zero. The final list includes cobalt blue center.

title: Tectonic Plate Strain Mapper
spec: Create a geophysical analysis script containing the function `map(faults)`. The input is a list of tuples representing fault lines, containing a region name, a slip distance, a pressure reading, and a seismic tremor count. Generate an eight element tuple of lists. First, list all region names. Second, list all tremor counts. Third, isolate the region names of active faults where the tremor count exceeds fifty. Fourth, extract the slip distances for these active faults. Fifth, convert the slip distances to millimeters by multiplying by ten. Sixth, extract the pressure readings for the active faults. Seventh, calculate a rupture risk index by multiplying each active pressure reading by one point five. Eighth, create a warning alert for each active fault by appending the phrase high risk to the region name. Return the eight collected lists in a tuple. Include a driver block setting up dummy fault data. Example input: san andreas, five, twenty, sixty. The eighth list will hold san andreas high risk.

title: Sourdough Starter Microbiome
spec: Write a fermentation tracking module with the function `analyze(cultures)`. The input is a list of tuples representing yeast samples, containing a strain identifier, a reproduction rate, an acid production level, and an inactivity metric. Output an eight part tuple of lists. First, extract all strain identifiers. Second, extract all inactivity metrics. Third, filter the strain identifiers for vigorous cultures where the inactivity metric is below five. Fourth, extract the reproduction rates for these vigorous cultures. Fifth, estimate the daily expansion by multiplying each vigorous reproduction rate by twenty four. Sixth, extract the acid production levels of the vigorous cultures. Seventh, calculate the tanginess score by adding ten to each vigorous acid production level. Eighth, formulate a bakery label for each vigorous culture by joining the strain identifier with the word active. Return these eight sequences. Provide a main execution block to test the tracker. Example input: san francisco, two, five, one. The final list includes san francisco active.

title: Blacksmith Forge Temperatures
spec: Implement a metallurgical logging script featuring the function `forge(metals)`. The input is a sequence of tuples representing heated metals, containing a metal type, a core temperature, a cooling time, and an oxidation level. The script must return eight distinct lists in a tuple. First, gather all metal types. Second, gather all oxidation levels. Third, identify the metal types of clean heats where the oxidation level is strictly less than two. Fourth, extract the core temperatures for these clean heats. Fifth, convert the temperatures from celsius to fahrenheit by multiplying by one point eight and adding thirty two. Sixth, extract the cooling times for the clean heats. Seventh, calculate the required quenching liquid volume by halving each clean cooling time. Eighth, generate a workbench tag for each clean heat by appending the word ready to the metal type. Return the full tuple of lists. Write a driver routine with sample forge records. Example input: iron, eight hundred, twenty, one. The final list contains iron ready.

title: Bookbinding Thread Stitcher
spec: Develop a traditional crafting script starting with the function `stitch(signatures)`. The input is a list of tuples representing book sections, containing a paper type, a page count, a thread length, and a tear defect count. Produce an eight list tuple for the bindery. First, retrieve all paper types. Second, retrieve all tear defect counts. Third, filter the paper types for pristine sections that have exactly zero tears. Fourth, extract the page counts of these pristine sections. Fifth, calculate the spine thickness by multiplying each pristine page count by zero point one. Sixth, extract the thread lengths for the pristine sections. Seventh, determine the required beeswax coating by multiplying each pristine thread length by zero point zero five. Eighth, format a binding instruction for each pristine section by joining the paper type with the phrase fold center. Return the tuple containing these eight lists. Add a small main section to process example sections. Example input: vellum, sixteen, thirty, zero. The eighth list includes vellum fold center.

title: Seismograph Tremor Validator
spec: Create a geological monitoring script with the function `validate(events)`. The input is a list of tuples representing seismic events, containing a location string, a peak amplitude, a duration in seconds, and an interference noise level. Generate an eight element tuple of lists. First, list all location strings. Second, list all noise levels. Third, isolate the locations of clear signals where the noise level is below ten. Fourth, extract the peak amplitudes for these clear signals. Fifth, calculate the energy release by squaring each clear peak amplitude. Sixth, extract the durations for the clear signals. Seventh, compute the extended monitoring time by adding sixty to each clear duration. Eighth, create an official log entry for each clear signal by appending the phrase confirmed event to the location string. Return the eight collected lists in a tuple. Include a driver block setting up dummy tremor data. Example input: fault line alpha, five, twelve, two. The final list holds fault line alpha confirmed event.

title: Gemstone Facet Analyzer
spec: Write a lapidary evaluation module utilizing the function `evaluate(stones)`. The input is a sequence of tuples representing uncut gems, containing a mineral name, a primary angle, a light refraction index, and an internal inclusion count. Output an eight part tuple of lists. First, extract all mineral names. Second, extract all internal inclusion counts. Third, filter the mineral names for flawless stones where the inclusion count is strictly zero. Fourth, extract the primary angles for these flawless stones. Fifth, calculate the optimal cutting offset by subtracting five from each flawless primary angle. Sixth, extract the light refraction indices of the flawless stones. Seventh, determine the brilliance score by multiplying each flawless refraction index by one hundred. Eighth, construct a jeweler certificate string for each flawless stone by joining the mineral name with the word flawless. Return these eight sequences. Provide a main execution block to test the analyzer. Example input: diamond, forty, two point four, zero. The final list includes diamond flawless.

title: Fungal Mycelium Network
spec: Implement a mycological mapping script featuring the function `map(nodes)`. The input is a list of tuples representing fungal growth points, containing a species string, a growth rate, a moisture level, and a dead end flag. The script must return eight distinct lists in a tuple. First, gather all species strings. Second, gather all dead end flags. Third, identify the species of active nodes where the dead end flag is zero. Fourth, extract the growth rates for these active nodes. Fifth, estimate the weekly expansion by multiplying each active growth rate by seven. Sixth, extract the moisture levels for the active nodes. Seventh, calculate the required nutrient drop by multiplying each active moisture level by zero point eight. Eighth, generate a laboratory observation for each active node by appending the phrase spreading rapidly to the species string. Return the full tuple of lists. Write a driver routine with sample fungal records. Example input: shiitake, three, eighty, zero. The final list contains shiitake spreading rapidly.

title: Orchestral Score Arranger
spec: Develop a musical notation script starting with the function `arrange(notes)`. The input is a list of tuples representing musical passages, containing an instrument name, a base frequency, a duration in beats, and an out of range error count. Produce an eight list tuple for the conductor. First, retrieve all instrument names. Second, retrieve all error counts. Third, filter the instrument names for playable passages that have zero out of range errors. Fourth, extract the base frequencies of these playable passages. Fifth, transpose the frequencies up a perfect fifth by multiplying each by one point five. Sixth, extract the durations for the playable passages. Seventh, calculate the time in seconds by multiplying each playable duration by zero point five. Eighth, format a sheet music header for each playable passage by joining the instrument name with the phrase section cue. Return the tuple containing these eight lists. Add a small main section to process example passages. Example input: cello, two hundred, four, zero. The eighth list includes cello section cue.
